subject: SLO metric thresholds & maintenance communication protocol (MSA / Order Form redlines)
body:
From: Tariq Alvi <tariq@lumenix.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amelia Ross <amelia@lumenix.com>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed SLO thresholds + maintenance comms for MSA/Order Form

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our contracts team dug into the MSA + draft Order Form and surfaced a couple of items we need clarified before we can route to procurement: primarily the uptime measurement window, the service credit calculation, and the advance notice window for maintenance that could affect multi-region routing.

Quick summary of our asks (see attached PDF for a table):
- Define uptime measurement window (30d rolling vs. calendar month)
- Clarify when a service credit is triggered (thresholds at 99.5/99.0/95.0) and whether credits are prorated by impacted region
- Align on response times for P1/P2 incidents and optional on-call escalation contact
- Maintenance: minimum notice (7 / 14 / 30 days), blackout periods, and whether emergency maintenance counts as an exclusion

Can you confirm Redwood's recommended defaults and call out anything you expect operations to be unable to commit to at scale? We want to avoid open-ended language in the OF that would hold us up for legal review.

Regards,
Tariq
Head of Cloud Ops, Lumenix
[attachment: lumenix_proposed_svc_credits.pdf (pdf)]

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Tariq Alvi <tariq@lumenix.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLO thresholds + maintenance comms for MSA/Order Form

Tariq — thanks for the clear list, this helps. I pulled in Lauren for legal redlines and Marissa for ops impact; below is our initial read. I'm including suggested wording we can push into the Order Form to avoid ambiguous phrasing.

1) Uptime measurement window
- Ops recommendation: 30-day rolling measurement to reflect real usage patterns.
- Legal note: if Lumenix prefers calendar month for billing simplicity, we can add a clause that defines "Billing Period" and allows either party to agree in advance.

Suggested OF clause (draft): "Availability will be measured over a 30-day rolling window (each a 'Measurement Window'). Availability % = (Total Available Minutes in the Measurement Window / Total Scheduled Minutes in the Measurement Window) * 100."

2) Service credit triggers
- Redwood suggests tiered credits at <=99.5 (5% credit), <=99.0 (10% credit), <=95.0 (25% credit) prorated by impacted region and by resource group.
- Marissa: ops can support regional granularity provided impacted traffic isolation can be demonstrated (routing/region tags).

3) Response times and on-call escalation
- Proposed: P1 initial response <= 30 minutes, P1 mitigation/update every 1 hour until resolution; P2 initial response <= 2 hours.
- We propose providing a named escalation contact as part of Dedicated commitments; Hosted customers get standard support tiers per OF.

4) Maintenance windows / notices
- Suggested baseline: Planned maintenance notifications >= 14 days; emergency maintenance as reasonably required with < 24 hours notice but does not count as an availability breach if pre-defined emergency criteria are met.
- Blackout periods: support for customer-requested blackout windows to avoid planned changes during agreed business-critical dates; these are mutually agreed in writing.

Next steps I suggest: Lauren to propose redline language for the MSA/OF, Marissa to map operational constraints and produce a short runbook on how region-impact is verified. Can we schedule a 30-min sync tomorrow to walk Lumenix through the proposed wording?

— Jonas
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Tariq Alvi <tariq@lumenix.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Amelia Ross <amelia@lumenix.com>
Date: Thu, 10 May 2028 13:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLO thresholds + maintenance comms for MSA/Order Form

Tariq and team — looping legal in. I've attached a draft Order Form redline that converts the bullets into contract-ready language and limits open-ended terms. Key legal points:

- Measurement window: Accepting 30-day rolling is fine; we'll add an explicit definition for "Measurement Window" and "Scheduled Minutes."
- Credit cap: we usually cap annual credits to the lesser of 100% of one month’s fees or the sum of monthly credits for the period. Please let us know if Lumenix needs a different ceiling for regulatory reasons.
- Emergency maintenance: define the emergency carve-out narrowly (security vulnerability or immediate customer data risk) and require Redwood to notify customer within 4 hours of event classification.
- Evidence & verification: include a clause that Redwood will provide incident evidence (metrics, traces) within 10 business days of a credit claim; if dispute remains, both parties agree to an independent third-party audit scope for the Measurement Window.

I've tracked suggested edits in redline_orderform_draft.docx. If Lumenix wants different credit % or different caps, list preferred alternatives and we'll run a financial impact assessment.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
[attachment: redline_orderform_draft.docx (docx)]

---

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Tariq Alvi <tariq@lumenix.com>
Date: Fri, 11 May 2028 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLO thresholds + maintenance comms for MSA/Order Form

All — ops notes from my side:
- Regional granularity: we can scope credits/impact to specific regions if Lumenix can provide the footprint (region tags + minimum traffic volume threshold). Without that, proving isolation is operationally heavy.
- Monitoring & evidence: we'll export the availability dashboard slice for the Measurement Window; for credit claims we need a 10-business-day SLA to investigate and prepare evidence.
- Maintenance: 14 days notice is fine for planned maintenance; for emergency maintenance we need a succinct definition and an after-action report within 72 hours.

I'll prepare a one-pager runbook for how we evaluate "impacted region" (routing rules, traffic sampling, cache invalidation checks) and attach to the OF as an appendix. That will reduce back-and-forth during claims.

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

---

From: Tariq Alvi <tariq@lumenix.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Amelia Ross <amelia@lumenix.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 12 May 2028 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposed SLO thresholds + maintenance comms for MSA/Order Form

Jonas / Lauren / Marissa — thanks for the quick turnaround and clear redlines. Lumenix prefers calendar-month billing for our internal chargeback model, but we can accept a 30-day rolling Measurement Window in the OF provided the "Billing Period" is defined as calendar month for invoicing and the measurement math is reconciled to that window for crediting.

On credits: we propose adjusting the mid-tier trigger to <=99.2 rather than 99.0; otherwise the proposed %s look reasonable.

Action items we’ll take:
- Amelia (cc) will do a quick review of Lauren's redline and return marked alternatives by EOD Mon.
- We’re happy to do the footprint export for the regional isolation test; I’ll have infra send that once we confirm a mutual NDA carve-out for logs.
- Please send a calendar invite for a 30-minute sync next week to finalize the redline language and walk through Marissa's runbook.

Thanks again — Tariq
Head of Cloud Ops, Lumenix Inc
